hints.title: Interleaved Execution Time Attribution Obstacle
hints.text: Function calls interrupt each other when nested. How can recording the last recorded timestamp allow you to credit execution slices to whichever function is actively running?

hints.title: Active Call-Frame Time Slicing Invariant
hints.text: Track the active function ID on top of a call stack and update its exclusive time by elapsed intervals before pushing or after popping.

hints.title: Timestamp Interval Attribution Procedure
hints.text: Initialize res of size n with zeros. Parse logs: on 'start', if call stack is non-empty, add timestamp - prevTime to top function. Push function ID and set prevTime = timestamp. On 'end', pop function ID, add timestamp - prevTime + 1 to its total, and set prevTime = timestamp + 1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: L: number of log entries (1 <= L <= 500)
complexity.notes: Single pass attributing elapsed intervals to active top-of-stack functions.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Summing start and end times naively counts child execution time toward parent functions multiple times.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Call stack tracking mirrors thread execution in linear time with O(L) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Accounting for inclusive end timestamps where an 'end' log includes the entire second (ts - prev_time + 1).
